headline: A 2018 law directs the Department of Transportation to coordinate efforts against human trafficking in transportation and set up an advisory committee on the issue.
what_it_does: The law requires the Department of Transportation to name an official who coordinates anti-trafficking work across its agencies and with other federal agencies, while considering how trafficking differs across transportation modes. It expands an existing trucking safety outreach program and a commercial driver's license financial assistance program to cover recognizing, preventing, and reporting human trafficking. It also creates an advisory committee that recommends actions for the department and develops best practices for states and local transportation stakeholders.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial truck drivers and commercial driver's license holders
who_it_affects.how: The outreach and education and license-related assistance programs now cover training on recognizing, preventing, and reporting human trafficking.

who_it_affects.group: Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration and other Department of Transportation modal administrations
who_it_affects.how: They must coordinate anti-trafficking efforts under a designated department official and consider the challenges specific to their transportation modes.

who_it_affects.group: State and local transportation agencies and other transportation stakeholders
who_it_affects.how: They may receive best practices developed by the new advisory committee for combating human trafficking.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 3, 2018; the official summary does not list any separate effective dates or deadlines for the requirements.
